discoveries.explanation: Best guess, with low confidence: an eclipsing binary. A dip of 13.803% repeats every 4.5073 days and lasts about 1.9 hours. The object is too large to be a planet; could be a small star or a blended signal. Dip depth 13.803% on a 2.23 R_sun star implies about 8.07 Jupiter radii (90.5 Earth radii). That is bigger than any known planet (limit 2 Jupiter radii), so it is too large to be a planet. Alternate dips match and there is no strong second dip, so this is not a sure binary either. This matches TIC 219707463 (TESS EB catalogue) on the TESS Eclipsing Binary catalogue (Prsa et al. 2022) (same period).
